title: MineWorldGen Project
description: The single project format shared by the web editor and both export paths. A project is design data, not Minecraft data: it is never read by the game. Procedural Export analyses it into generator parameters; Exact Export additionally compiles its map layers into a coordinate-addressable field.

format.description: Project format version. Bumped only on breaking changes; the editor migrates older versions on load.

world.description: Dimension geometry. Mirrors the datapack config so a project round-trips through either export path unchanged.

seed.description: 0 means the seed entered at world creation is used. Any other value pins the procedural fields; user map layers are deterministic regardless.

map.description: The drawn design surface. Its size is NOT the world size: outside it, procedural generation continues forever.

width.description: West-east extent of the design surface, in Minecraft blocks.

height.description: North-south extent of the design surface, in Minecraft blocks.

origin.description: Minecraft coordinate that the centre of the map corresponds to.

resolution.description: Blocks per map cell. The stored grid is width/resolution by height/resolution cells. Larger values shrink the project file and the compiled field at the cost of detail; the compiler interpolates between cells either way.

edge_mode.description: How the design surface meets the infinite procedural world. 'falloff' fades the user constraint weight to zero over edge_falloff blocks, so the boundary is invisible. 'hard' keeps full weight to the last cell, which is only sensible when the map edge is deep ocean anyway.

edge_falloff.description: Width of the transition band in blocks, measured inward from the map edge.

generator.description: Procedural generator parameters. Identical in meaning to pack/config.json, minus its 'mode' key: whether anything is written at all is decided by export.mode. Values outside their range are clamped at compile time, never rejected.

mode.description: 'vanilla' writes no world generation files, so terrain is identical to vanilla. 'procedural' emits a pure datapack whose parameters were analysed from the map; absolute positions are not reproduced. 'exact' emits a datapack plus a companion mod that samples the map layers at real X/Z, preserving position and orientation.

field_precision.description: Exact Export only. Cell size in blocks of the compiled field shipped to the game. Independent of map.resolution so a finely drawn map can ship coarsely.

editor.description: UI state. Ignored by both compilers; preserved so reopening a project restores the workspace.

layers.description: Every layer is an independent field over the same grid. Nothing is derived from anything else: in particular land/sea is never inferred from elevation, so land below sea level and ocean above it are both representable.

land.description: 0 = ocean, 1 = land. Authoritative; elevation has no say in it.

elevation.description: Target surface height as a real Minecraft Y coordinate, not an abstract 0-1 value. A target, not a hard heightmap: the generator adds erosion and detail on top of it.

temperature.description: Climate temperature in the -0.5 to 2.0 range used by the biome source.

biome.description: Palette-indexed vanilla biome id. Where set, it pins biome, land/sea character and the climate values needed to reach it; other brushes must not overwrite that until the biome itself is cleared.

feature.description: Bit flags marking terrain intent such as volcano, atoll, fjord or arc. Additive; several flags may apply to one cell.

dtype.description: Storage type of one cell. Chosen per layer for size: land fits in a byte, elevation needs 16 bits to cover the full Y range, biome indexes a palette.

encoding.description: 'raw' is a plain base64 typed array. 'deflate' is base64 of the deflate-compressed array, which is what the editor writes by default. 'rle' is run-length pairs for layers that are mostly one value. 'sparse' stores only the cells that differ from the default, as index/value pairs, and suits the biome layer where most of the map is unpainted.

data.description: Base64 payload. Row-major, x fastest, starting at the north-west cell.

default.description: Value for cells absent from a sparse payload, and the value a cleared cell returns to.

scale.description: Multiplier applied when decoding, so a fractional field can be stored as integers. stored * scale + offset = real value.

palette.description: Biome layer only. Maps a stored index to a vanilla biome id such as minecraft:plains. Index 0 is reserved for 'unpainted'.

flags.description: Feature layer only. Names the meaning of each bit, least significant first.

strength.description: How firmly this layer overrides the procedural field. 1.0 lets the drawn value dominate, 0.0 makes it advisory only. Hidden behind an advanced toggle in the editor; land and biome default to hard, temperature to soft.

size.description: Diameter in Minecraft blocks, matching the map's own units.

mode.description: Elevation brushes only. raise and lower move relative to the current value; raise_to and lower_to move toward a target without crossing it; set drives the centre to the target outright.

amount.description: Blocks of change per application for raise and lower.

slope_strength.description: Falloff applied while the brush is being used, not afterwards. 0 gives a flat-topped stamp with an abrupt edge; higher values spread the change into a smooth slope across the brush radius, the way a terrain editor does. Applied at stroke time, never as a post-process.

flow.description: Fraction of the full effect applied per stroke step, so dragging builds up gradually instead of saturating instantly.
